title: SLO alignment matrix and quarterly batching playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments we lack a succinct mechanism to prioritize reliability work against feature roadmaps and provide predictable error-budget reallocation. Current playbooks are scattered, and engineering teams respond ad-hoc to SLO burns which causes inconsistent customer outcomes.

Goal: Deliver an "alignment matrix" (single-pane decision guide) plus a Quarterly Batching Playbook that: 1) maps SLO/SLI characteristics to initiative priority, 2) prescribes tranche-based error budget allocations and safe reallocation gates, and 3) defines a repeatable quarterly cadence ("maintenance batching") where reliability micro-initiatives are scheduled, measured and rolled out alongside feature launches.

Why this is different: Instead of a static error-budget handbook, this playbook ties error-budget allocation directly to product impact signals (customer-visible severity, revenue exposure, compliance sensitivity) and operational signals (burn-rate velocity, previous regression risk). It operationalizes a lightweight stewardship model so teams can trade budget across tranches without loss of governance.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Alignment matrix doc (Confluence) exists and maps at least 6 representative SLIs to 4 product-impact axes and prescribes priority buckets (Critical, High, Medium, Low).
A2: Quarterly Batching template with schedule slots (2 maintenance sprints per quarter) and owner roles (Tranche Steward, Release Gatekeeper) is published and linked in the Console runbook.

A3: Playbook contains concrete reallocation policy: thresholds for automatic freeze, temporary reallocation window, and escalation paths. Examples for two scenarios (hosted API latency spike, Dedicated capacity regression) included.

A4: Two teams (runtime and console) run a pilot using the template for Q2 initiative planning; pilot retros show measurable reduction in emergency rollbacks (target: -30% rollback incidents during pilot).
A5: Dashboard panels in Grafana linked from the playbook show SLI trends, burn rate, and active tranche assignments; alerts for gate breaches configured with runbook links.

decision_log: Decision 2026-02-03: Use a hybrid policy — automated freeze for extreme burns, steward approval for moderate reallocations.
Decision 2026-02-20: Represent SLO priority as a 2-axis matrix: Product Impact (Customer Visibility x Revenue/Compliance Sensitivity) and Operational Risk (Burn Velocity x Regression Probability).
Decision 2026-03-01: Pilot cadence = 2 maintenance sprints per quarter; each sprint supports up to 3 micro-initiatives per team.
comments: Priya (Reliability): 'We should include explicit examples for Dedicated capacity transients — those are common false alarms during scaling events.'

risks: Risk: Overly permissive reallocation may mask systemic regressions; mitigated by mandatory post-mortem for reallocations >72h.
Risk: Insufficient observability for some SLIs — addressed by ENG-20482 and a measurement spike ahead of pilot.
